title: The activity, divergence, and evolutionary degradation of modern-day homing endonucleases and behavior of their reconstructed ancestors.
data_url: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/Z4WCBW (Harvard Dataverse, CC0) plus the journal supplement zip (Europe PMC)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Unpacked the supplement (4.9 MB zip -> 'Supplementary Information.zip') and opened the key table 'Original 371 LHE Sequences, Targets, and Quantified Expression and Activity Values.xlsx' in pandas: exactly 371 rows x 14 columns, one sheet. Counted non-null labels: 307 rows with 'Quantified % Expression' (0-39.3% of cells, 91 zeros, 216 above zero) and 188 rows with 'Quantified Cleavage Assay 1 - Mg/Ca Ratio' (0-0.9; only 27 above the paper's 0.1 activity threshold, 20 above 0.2). Confirmed inputs are present in the table: full protein sequence ('ORF AA', 369 non-null, 241-444 residues), coding DNA, and a 60-base-pair 'Predicted DNA Target Site' for all 371 rows (341 unique). 371 unique GenBank GI numbers, 132 organisms, 2 duplicate protein sequences, an assay-batch/date column for all 188 cleavage rows. Also checked the companion files: Fig3a_sequenceInfoTable_n390.csv (390 sequences), SuppFigS3_sequenceInfoTable_n633.csv (633), three alignment FASTA files (390/631/1140 records) and the README - these carry sequences only, no activity values. Queried the Harvard Dataverse API: the dataset is CC0 but contains only ONE file, a 101 MB PowerPoint of flow-cytometry plots (not downloaded, over the 50 MB cap).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The assay definitions (percent of cells in the full-length anti-Myc expression gate; cleavage = median A647 signal ratio magnesium/calcium, so 1 minus that ratio is the fraction of cut substrate) come from the methods and figure legends. The pipeline numbers (371 candidates found, 30 failed synthesis leaving 341, 307 successfully subcloned and assayed, 625-sequence expanded bioinformatic set) are from the methods. I did not open the 101 MB flow-cytometry PowerPoint or the 4.7 MB supplementary figures PDF.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplement zip downloads freely from Europe PMC and the Harvard Dataverse deposit is CC0 with no access request; I opened both listings. Note the data availability statement promises sequencing output and gels, but Dataverse holds only a 101 MB PowerPoint of flow plots.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Both labels are literal columns in one spreadsheet: 'Quantified % Expression' and 'Quantified Cleavage Assay 1 - Mg/Ca Ratio'. Nothing has to be constructed. Verified in the file.

a3_inputs_present.note: Full amino-acid sequence, coding DNA, and the 60-base-pair predicted DNA target site are all in the same row; no accession lookups needed. Verified in the file.

a4_units_stated.note: Column headers name the units (percent of cells expressing; magnesium/calcium median-signal ratio) and the figure legends define both precisely. Verified in file plus paper.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS. The whole experiment is 371 candidate genes, of which only 307 have an expression number and 188 a cleavage number, and only 27 of those 188 are active above the paper's own 0.1 threshold. The checklist fails anything under ~1,500 labelled rows for regression or ~400 for classification; 307 and 188 are below both. Effective sample size is smaller still: 132 source organisms with up to 20 near-relatives each (20 Podospora anserina, 20 Fusarium graminearum), so sequence-identity clustering would leave far fewer independent groups. No public source of more LAGLIDADG homing endonuclease activity measurements exists to top it up, and the companion 390/633/1140-sequence files carry no activity values. Counted directly in the spreadsheet.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 224 KB spreadsheet plus ~0.6 MB of FASTA
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; the only large file is a 101 MB flow-cytometry PowerPoint that the modelling would not need.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Exact agreement: the paper says 307 quantified expression values and 188 quantified cleavage values, and the file has exactly 307 and 188 non-null. Best count-matching I have seen in this batch.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are direct flow-cytometry measurements on yeast displaying each protein, not another model's output and not computable from the sequence. One caveat: the DNA target each enzyme was tested against was inferred from the host gene flanking the intron, so a zero-cleavage row may mean a wrong target rather than a dead enzyme.

existing_models.name: Machine-learning meganuclease design method (BMC Bioinformatics 2014, 'Efficient design of meganucleases using a machine learning approach'; Cellectis-derived I-CreI engineering data)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported predicting active meganucleases for 53 new DNA targets with up to a four-fold higher design success rate than physical in-silico models; I read only the search-returned abstract summary, not the paper, so I cannot state the split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not read; the broader literature (homing endonuclease reviews found in the same search) states that context-dependent effects of changing residues in the DNA-binding and catalytic domains remain unpredictable, so empirical cleavage testing is still required.

existing_models.name: LAHEDES (LAGLIDADG homing endonuclease database and engineering server) - a rules/alignment-based web server, not a trained model
existing_models.score_and_split: No published accuracy number retrieved; it scores candidate protein-DNA contacts from known structures rather than learning from activity data.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) for the enzyme sequence, plus a DNA language model such as Nucleotide Transformer for the 60-base-pair target
backbone.hardware: CPU only; embedding 371 sequences of ~300 residues takes minutes
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; the data is CC0

integration.partner_dataset: Protein Data Bank / AlphaFold DB structures of the nine reference LAGLIDADG endonucleases (PDB 4YIT, 4YIS, 4YHX, 3R7P, 3QQY, 5ESP, 5E5O) and Pfam PF00961 family members
integration.join_key: GenBank GI number -> protein accession -> UniProt/Pfam; structural homologs by sequence alignment
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the pattern of mutations that degrade a selfish gene's enzyme activity fall on the DNA-contacting surface or on the fold, and can a sequence model tell a decaying pseudo-enzyme from a live one? - a good question that 188 measurements cannot answer with statistical confidence.

controls.positive_control: The two previously characterized enzymes I-OnuI and I-SmaMI are included as reference bars with known high expression and activity; presence of the LAGLIDADG catalytic motif should be learnable from sequence.
controls.negative_control: 46 clones with zero surface expression and 56 with exactly zero cleavage provide genuine negatives; label shuffling is cheap on a table this small.
controls.external_validation: None found. There is no second public dataset of measured LAGLIDADG homing endonuclease expression or cleavage; engineered-meganuclease activity data is proprietary (Cellectis, Precision BioSciences, bluebird bio).

honest_claim_h3: Among 307 fungal and algal organelle-genome LAGLIDADG endonuclease genes that one lab could synthesize and clone, a sequence model could at best say which ones display as full-length protein on yeast and which of 188 cut a computationally inferred target - a claim resting on fewer than 30 active examples.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a homing endonuclease's protein sequence and its DNA target to predict whether the protein folds and cuts that target.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per endonuclease gene: the 241-444 residue protein sequence, its coding DNA, and the 60-base-pair DNA site it is predicted to attack. 371 rows exist, 307 with an expression measurement and 188 with a cutting measurement (counts verified in the file).
plain_idea.predict: Two numbers measured by flow cytometry on yeast displaying each enzyme: the percentage of cells showing full-length protein on the surface, and the fraction of tethered DNA target cut (one minus the magnesium/calcium fluorescence ratio).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups that repurpose these natural enzymes as gene-editing tools (the Stoddard lab at Fred Hutch, bluebird bio) currently synthesize and screen hundreds of candidates to find ~10% that work; a pre-screen would save that cost. Even a failed model would show how much of enzyme decay is readable from sequence alone.

more_or_better_data.why: These are 307 natural, wild-type enzymes from 132 organisms measured in one consistent assay, whereas the 2014 machine-learning meganuclease work used engineered I-CreI variants of a single scaffold - genuinely different and complementary data, but only 307 rows of it.

confidence_score.why: The spreadsheet holds one value per enzyme per assay with no replicate columns, so per-prediction uncertainty could only come from model ensembling, not from measured noise.

models_beatable.why: The only named prior model is from 2014, pre-dates protein language models, was built on proprietary single-scaffold engineering data, and its weights are not public - but with 188 cleavage rows there is no honest way to demonstrate a win.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The 2014 model cannot be run as a baseline (closed weights, different scaffold, different assay), so the condition 'the existing model is our baseline, measuring the same quantity the same way' fails outright.

ml_idea: Freeze ESM-2 embeddings of each endonuclease sequence (optionally concatenated with a DNA language model embedding of the 60-base-pair target) and fit a small head to predict (a) percent full-length surface expression and (b) fraction of DNA target cut, evaluated with leave-one-sequence-cluster-out splits so that near-identical fungal homologs do not straddle train and test. Rejected on sample size: 307 expression and 188 cleavage measurements, with 27 actives, cannot support this honestly.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed beyond the pandas reads I ran: 371 sequences of ~300 residues through ESM-2 small on CPU is a few minutes, and the whole dataset is a 224 KB spreadsheet. Effort was never the problem here.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count non-null label cells in the one supplementary spreadsheet - I did this, and it returns 307 expression and 188 cleavage values with 27 actives, which kills the project in ten minutes.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 on sample size. This is otherwise an unusually clean candidate: one 371-row spreadsheet, protein sequence and 60-base-pair DNA target in the same row, units stated, counts matching the paper exactly (307 and 188), CC0 licence, genuine negatives, and no modern machine-learning model on this task. But the labels number 307 (surface expression) and 188 (DNA cleavage), with only 27 enzymes active above the authors' own 0.1 threshold, which is under the checklist's ~400-row floor even for a pure classification task. Sequence redundancy makes it worse - up to 20 near-relatives from a single organism - so a leakage-safe leave-one-cluster-out split would leave only a handful of independent test groups, and there is no second public dataset of measured LAGLIDADG endonuclease activity to pool with. Worth remembering if this group releases the later, larger screen.
